title: Large dust grains and a possible dust trap in the polar circumbinary disc of HD 98800B
question: What is the millimetre/centimetre dust spectral index, level of grain growth, non-thermal emission contribution, and origin of the azimuthal asymmetry in the polar circumbinary disc of HD 98800B?

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image new VLA 6.8 mm and 3 cm observations and measure fluxes, plus extract archival ALMA 3 mm flux
recipe.method: Calibrate VLA Q and X band data with CASA and the VLA pipeline, perform one round of phase-only self-calibration, image with tclean (natural weighting at 6.8 mm, briggs robust=0.5 at 3 cm, hobgom deconvolver), measure 3 cm fluxes with imfit, and fit a Gaussian to unresolved archival ALMA 3 mm emission.
key_parameters: Q band: natural weighting, hobgom deconvolver; X band: briggs weighting with robust = 0.5, hobgom deconvolver
assumptions: Absolute flux calibration uncertainty is 5% at ALMA 3 mm and VLA 3 cm, and 10% at VLA 6.8 mm

recipe.goal: Estimate disc dust mass of HD 98800B from 6.8 mm flux
recipe.method: Calculate optically thin dust mass from the 6.8 mm VLA flux using standard blackbody relation and bootstrap 1000 realizations to propagate parameter uncertainties
assumptions: Optically thin emission at 6.8 mm, distance d = 45 pc, dust opacity at 6.8 mm varied log-uniformly between 0.03 and 0.3 g cm^-2, dust temperature varied uniformly between 50 and 100 K

recipe.goal: Measure azimuthal asymmetry significance in VLA 6.8 mm and 8.8 mm images
recipe.method: Compare peak brightness on the east and west sides of the disc relative to the image rms noise: (I_max,East - I_max,West) / sqrt(2 * sigma_rms^2)

recipe.goal: Derive pairwise mm/cm spectral indices and fit multi-wavelength SED model for dust and non-thermal contamination
recipe.method: Compute pairwise spectral indices alpha = log(F_nu1/F_nu2)/log(nu1/nu2) and fit all photometry at lambda >= 500 um with a 7-parameter model combining a sigmoid-transitioning double power-law dust component and a single power-law contamination component using MCMC
key_parameters: 7 free parameters: F_0,dust, eta_-, eta_+, nu_dust, gamma, F_0,cont, alpha_cont
assumptions: Non-thermal contamination is represented by a single power law; alpha_cont <= eta_+ <= eta_- enforced

recipe.goal: Test illumination and optically thick inner wall explanations for the azimuthal asymmetry
recipe.method: Calculate binary orbital phases at the epochs of ALMA 1.3 mm and VLA 6.8 and 8.8 mm observations, and generate 3D radiative transfer simulated images at 1.3 mm, 6.8 mm, and 8.8 mm with MCFOST convolved with the observed beams
key_parameters: Disc radial extent 2.5 to 4.6 au, inclination 26 deg, PA 16 deg, dust mass 5e-5 M_sun, stars placed 0.5 au above/below disc plane
assumptions: Far side of the disc is located on the east side in the test model; dust density distribution is azimuthally symmetric
